Issued at 120 AM CDT Wed Oct 21 2026

A weak cold front has been moving through central and northeastern 
SD and west central MN this morning. This cold front will not be 
cooling temperatures too much today, as highs in the upper 60s to 
low 70s will still be 10-15 degrees warmer than normal. This front 
will cause the winds to turn and be from the northeast to easterly 
during the day and then turn overnight to be from the south. The 
southerly winds will be bringing in warmer temperatures Thursday and 
Friday, with highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. These temperatures 
will be about 20-25 degrees warmer than normal for this time of the 
year, and some areas will get close to and potentially break record 
warm temperatures. 

While high pressure develops over the Great Lakes to the east, a 
surface low pressure will develop over NV and move to the north 
northeast over western MN and then into Manitoba Canada Thursday 
into Saturday. With these two strong pressure centers on opposite 
sides of SD, the pressure gradient over the state will tighten. This 
will cause winds to strengthen Thursday through Friday night over 
the state, starting in central SD Thursday afternoon and spreading 
east overnight into Friday. While Thursday's winds will be strong, 
with gust up to 35 mph possible. Friday will have the strongest 
winds. There is a 30-60% chance for winds to be sustained at or 
greater than 30 mph and 20-50% chance for gusts to be at or greater 
than 45 mph Friday through Saturday morning, mainly over the Coteau 
and areas west of the Missouri River. These strong winds will be 
increasing the fire weather concerns Thursday and Friday, as ground 
fuels are starting to cure and dry out in this fall weather. The 
grassland fire danger index values are forecast in the high category 
over portions of central SD Thursday and over central and 
northeastern SD Friday. The one thing stopping the fire danger from 
being greater is higher relative humidity values. Humidity values 
will be between 35-50% on Thursday and 35-55% on Friday, which will 
help to keep fires from starting. However if a fire were to start, 
it could become difficult to control or suppress. 

While the low pressure system will not be moving over SD, the fronts 
attached to it will be. A warm front will be moving over SD Thursday 
and sticking around into Friday, which is what is causing the warmer 
temperatures to move in SD during those days. The models are 
forecasting the warm front to start moving again on Friday, which 
will interact with moisture aloft to cause scattered showers and 
potentially even a storm or two. The models however vary where the 
warm front will be when rain starts to develop, and some of the 
models even have the rain missing the state. The next chance for 
rain showers from this system will be when a cold front moves 
through central and northeastern SD Friday night through Saturday. 
The models vary how long the cold front sticks around over eastern 
SD on Saturday, which then varies how much rainfall will occur. 
There is a 40-60% chance for 0.10 inch or more of rain over portions 
of eastern SD and west central MN from the Friday and Saturday rain, 
and a 20-40% chance for 0.25 inch over the same area. There is still 
lower confidence in the timing, track, and rainfall amounts due to 
the variability in the frontal boundaries in models. This will need 
to be watched in upcoming model runs to see if they start to show 
similar conditions. The one thing the models do agree on, is that 
there will be cold air moving in behind the cold front Saturday, 
which will cause temperatures during the weekend to be around normal 
for this time of the year.
